requirements.requirement: A local account named `opsadmin` exists on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then created locally. Successful pre- and post-restart checks against `/etc/passwd` and `id opsadmin` confirm that it exists and persisted across reboot.
`/home/opsadmin` is owned by `opsadmin:opsadmin` with mode 0700. Post-restart behavioral checks show owner read/write/traverse access and denial to `nobody`.
The account belongs to `wheel`, and the effective sudo policy before and after reboot grants `(ALL) ALL`.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, account, home-directory, and sudo state were directly observed and corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation, password assignment, ownership, mode, and SELinux-label restoration in cmd-503daa9d8c6d45c6 directly established the requested outcome and remained intentionally. The reboot scheduled by cmd-24adcb3909b34677 served the mandatory restart protocol; it was bounded and recovered cleanly. The changed boot identity is independently corroborated, with no failed services, package damage, unexpected socket exposure, or executor-created temporary residue after restart.
